rationale: Block 3 covers nociceptor types and peripheral sensitisation; this question tests recall of the two primary nociceptive afferent fibre types — a classic AS exam trap (Aδ vs C fibres).
Block 5 covers ascending spinal pathways; this question tests understanding of the spinothalamic tract decussation level — a common clinical viva trap.
Block 6 covers clinical pain assessment frameworks; this question tests application of the correct validated tool for a cognitively impaired patient — a real clinical decision.
Block 3 covers the WHO analgesic ladder; this question tests the key principle of the ladder's sequencing, a foundational prescribing concept.
Block 5 covers opioid receptor pharmacology; tests understanding of the primary opioid receptor mediating spinal analgesia — a common pharmacology viva question.
Block 7 covers adjuvant analgesics including gabapentinoids; tests application of the correct adjuvant choice for neuropathic pain — a key prescribing decision.
Block 3 covers goals of care in palliative medicine; tests understanding of the WHO definition and its ethical framework — foundational for AS8.4.
Block 4 covers opioid titration for cancer pain; tests the clinically critical 'by the clock' principle and breakthrough dose calculation — a common prescribing error source.
Block 8 covers symptom management in the last days of life; tests analysis of appropriate medication management during the active dying phase — a core AS8.5 competency.
